title: Chapter 15: Parfait
content: Chapter 15: Parfait

The Prometheus Project development team returned to the academy, showing various reactions as they faced the damaged and suspended Thunderbolt. The more favorable workers admired it, saying, “You really made it back.” Dr. Smith seemed unable to contain his excitement.
“Wow, Envy brought back some valuable data. The experimental machine got totally wrecked, but if we apply for a budget from the upper management and repair it, there won’t be any problems.”
He valued the data obtained this time more than the broken experimental machine itself.

However, there were also negative opinions. Some workers were downhearted, saying things like, “The repairs look tough,” “Please don’t let us lose all the weapons,” and “Looks like we’ll be pulling all-nighters for a while.”
Allison also took a negative stance.
“Sure, the data is valuable, but it’s unthinkable to throw away defense and specialize only in offense. If he’d taken even one hit, he would have been shot down!”
She clearly couldn’t believe Ren’s actions.
But Dr. Smith was different.

“From Envy’s point of view, taking one hit and it’s over was probably the same as when he was infantry. Still, it’s interesting. Cutting the magic power allocated to defense just because the weapons were ineffective? Wow, it’s great to have such an interesting pilot.”
Dr. Smith seemed delighted to have unintentionally obtained real combat data, and no matter how much Allison warned him, he refused to listen.
“If he keeps fighting like this, he’ll die someday.”
Allison’s words warning that they might lose an important pilot made Dr. Smith tilt his head in puzzlement.
“We can just prepare a new pilot. Isn’t that all?”
“You really are something... No, never mind.”
Allison had known Dr. Smith’s problem for some time. She stopped pointing it out and decided to have a constructive discussion.
“We’ll apply for a budget to repair the experimental machine, but be prepared to receive complaints from the upper management.”
“I think if we provide this data, they’ll be happy to prepare it. By the way, where is Envy? I want to hear about the combat from him.”
Allison let out a small sigh and then explained to Dr. Smith for the third time.
“I told you many times that he’s undergoing interrogation, didn’t I?”
“Huh? It’s not over yet? It’s just a story about a female student who tried and failed to stop the project.”
Dr. Smith’s dismissal of Louise’s involvement left Allison utterly exasperated.
“There was an agent inside the academy trying to stop our project. Shouldn’t we be more cautious?”
Dr. Smith shrugged and reluctantly agreed with Allison.
“You’re right. We need to be more vigilant from now on. We have to think of something.”
When I was released from interrogation, it was already past midnight. The academy was dark and silent.
I contacted Dr. Allison to inform her of my release, and she told me I could return to the dormitory today, so I was on my way back.
On the way, Lieutenant Hayase, who seemed to have been released before me, was sitting on a bench waiting.
“Good work.”
“Lieutenant Hayase, I sincerely thank you for saving my life this time—”
As I saluted, Lieutenant Hayase sighed with an exasperated look and motioned for me to stop with her hand.
“Formalities are tiring, so don’t bother. More importantly, since you came back safely, let’s celebrate.”
“A celebration, you say?”
I took her words at face value, but I didn’t know what to do to celebrate being safe.
When I was infantry, my squadmates would drink when we returned, but Lieutenant Hayase is underage.
She wouldn’t drink and party naked like us, right?
Well... she’s a bit rough around the edges, so I couldn’t be sure.
I started to feel a little uneasy.
Seeing my confusion, she grabbed my right wrist and started walking forcefully.
“Just follow me. I’ll teach you our custom.”
“Our custom at the academy... understood.”
I didn’t know if it was the whole academy’s custom or just within her battalion, but I should follow the customs of the Valkyries here.
When in Rome, do as the Romans do.
Besides, I was personally interested in the Valkyrie customs, and above all, Lieutenant Hayase had saved my life.
I couldn’t refuse her invitation.
“I’ll accompany you, Lieutenant Hayase.”
We arrived at a restaurant.
I was surprised it was open even after midnight, but Lieutenant Hayase, sensing my feelings, explained while looking at the menu.
“The owner here is thoughtful. On days when we go on sorties, he keeps the place open late.”
He keeps the restaurant open even when there are no customers to serve the Valkyries who returned safely.
“I see.”
Just as I was understanding why the restaurant was open so late, Lieutenant Hayase suddenly slammed the menu shut.
“All right, I’ve decided!”
After nodding once, she selected from the menu on the tablet on the table.
I thought she was inviting me to a meal, but for some reason, she chose from the dessert section.
“Lieutenant Hayase, wasn’t this supposed to be a meal?”
She answered while looking at the menu screen.
“We have a rule to eat sweets when we return safely. Or are you hungry? If so, we can order something else.”
“No, I ate emergency rations during interrogation, so I’m fine. Since it’s the academy’s custom, I’ll join you.”
Lieutenant Hayase turned to me after hearing my reply but seemed quite at a loss.
“Emergency rations? That awful emergency nutrition food, right? Didn’t they ask you what you wanted to eat during the interrogation? Or maybe, since you’re a guy, they didn’t ask you anything?”
She seemed worried that I might have been treated lightly during interrogation because I was male.
Of course, that wasn’t the case.
“They asked me what I wanted too. So I requested the chocolate-flavored emergency ration.”
Lieutenant Hayase made a slightly disgusted face, just like the Sabbat officers.
Is chocolate-flavored emergency ration no good? When I was infantry, it was such a tempting food that it even caused fights over it...
Lieutenant Hayase checked with me.
“You like chocolate?”
“Yes. The chocolate flavor is rare in emergency rations.”
“I see, then you’ll have chocolate.”
“Huh?”
Lieutenant Hayase quickly placed the order, and it seemed the kitchen had received it.
While waiting, I asked her a question.
“Lieutenant Hayase, may I ask you something?”
“What?”
“Why did you... help me?”
“Oh, that time? Because a Third Class appeared, it was just a side job. Just a side job.”
Lieutenant Hayase looked away from me—she lied.
We’ve talked many times, but for some reason, she always lies to me.
“No, not just during the operation. You’ve been moving around me for quite a while. You accompanied me unnaturally during the attack. Could it be that you were protecting me from Louise?”
Now that I think about it, I had encountered Lieutenant Hayase far too often.
The only ace I saw inside the academy wearing a colored cape was Lieutenant Hayase.
I hadn’t encountered any other ace.
Under such circumstances, would I repeatedly meet only Lieutenant Hayase?
Lieutenant Hayase turned her face away from my question and remained silent.

“Now that I think about it, I believe the time we met at the indoor pool late at night was also for me. There were actions that seemed like you came to see me, and above all, your advice was accurate. Didn’t you know what I was worried about?”
Considering today’s events, Louise giving me a self-help book was probably to confuse me.
Lieutenant Hayase, having noticed Louise’s intention, probably went all the way to the pool to advise my repeatedly failing self.
I looked at my right hand.

“The decisive factor was my right hand. Louise never touched my right hand. When she did, she resisted strongly. But Lieutenant Hayase grabbed it without hesitation. I still remember the feeling of Lieutenant Hayase’s strong hand, unafraid of me.”
Louise had been pretending in front of me but avoided my right arm made from Gijuu cells.
When she reluctantly held me with my right arm during the attack, she showed obvious dislike.
I don’t know if Lieutenant Hayase noticed, but rumors about what kind of surgery I had undergone had spread, so she probably knew.
And I had been suspicious of such a person and treated her terribly.
Louise had made me doubt Lieutenant Hayase, but that was no excuse.
“I’m ashamed I doubted you. You cared about me even during combat, didn’t you?”
Lieutenant Hayase looked down and reached out her hand.
“Enough... it’s fine now...”

“No, it’s not fine! When you came to save me, you knew everything about my situation. You cared about us during combat and listened to our conversations, didn’t you? Thanks to you, my life was saved. Lieutenant Hayase, thank you so much!”
I stood up and bowed deeply at the end, but Lieutenant Hayase didn’t seem pleased.
She also stood and protested to me.
“Don’t say that even if you know! And saying you knew everything makes me embarrassed! I thought you didn’t notice!”
I looked up, unable to understand why Lieutenant Hayase was embarrassed.
“Why? Your actions were more devoted than I deserved. Even though you cared so much, I was a fool to doubt you. Normally, it wouldn’t be strange if you abandoned me and shouted insults.”
Lieutenant Hayase pointed at me and waved her hands up and down.
“I did it on my own! Don’t worry about it!”
“No, that makes it worse. I can’t forgive myself for wasting your kindness.”
“Forget it! No, rather, please forget it! You seem dull, but why are you so sharp about this? Even if you noticed, keep it to yourself...”
Lieutenant Hayase’s words gradually lost strength.
When she collapsed onto the table, the ordered dish arrived.
The owner himself brought it—a jumbo parfait, strawberry and chocolate.
“Here’s your jumbo parfait, strawberry and chocolate. Now, mister, please sit down.”
“Y-yes.”
I sat down, watching Lieutenant Hayase carefully as the owner placed the chocolate parfait in front of me and left.
Parfait... I remembered it vaguely, but I had forgotten what it tasted like.
Lieutenant Hayase turned her face away from me, crossing her arms, looking embarrassed.
“...You can eat it. It’s on me.”
“No, I can’t accept that.”
“Superior’s order.”
Lieutenant Hayase gave me a resentful look, then sighed deeply before explaining why we were eating parfait.
“When we return safely, we eat sweets until we’re full... that’s our rule. Well, it differs by battalion. At that time, the higher-ranked person buys for the lower-ranked one.”
“I-I see. But I’m older than you?”
“I’m a lieutenant and you’re a warrant officer, right? Oh, don’t worry about the money. We get salaries and, I guess, some kind of reward for extermination.”
[img]https://i.imgur.com/qIDOyFb.jpeg
I didn’t know much about the Valkyries’ salary system, but everyone probably thought they earned a high income.
Having lived with them at the academy, I felt their lavish lifestyle.
“W-well then, I’ll have some.”
I scooped up a mountain of chocolate cream with my spoon and put it into my mouth.
Sweetness spread and quickly melted away.
I scooped up more and ate it.
Lieutenant Hayase scooped strawberry cream with her spoon and continued talking.

“Eat without worry. Normally, I’d eat with the whole battalion, but I was late because of the interrogation... Just so you know, I wasn’t waiting for you. It was just a coincidence that I happened to see you come out... huh!?”
Lieutenant Hayase looked surprised at me, who was eating the parfait with single-minded focus.
Realizing I’d been too absorbed in eating, I lifted my face and felt something trickle down my cheek.
I touched it with my hand.
It was liquid.
“Why are you crying?”
Lieutenant Hayase pointed out, and I finally realized I was crying.
“I don’t know... it’s just that it’s delicious.”
“You cried because it’s delicious? What have you been eating until now... Ah, never mind. Since you say emergency rations are tasty, you probably haven’t been eating anything good.”
Lieutenant Hayase came to her own conclusion before I could answer.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/tBOykyM.jpeg
Sure, when I was infantry, I mostly ate emergency rations on the battlefield, but I ate normal meals when back at base.
Even then, the meals were nutrition-focused and the taste was secondary, so my squadmates disliked them.
From there, memories of my comrades flooded back without end.
I wanted to let them eat this too.
Ah, I see... I... wanted to spend time with everyone again.
“I remembered my comrades.”
“Huh?”
“Before coming here, I was infantry. I always acted with my squadmates, and it was a comfortable squad.”
As I started talking, Lieutenant Hayase seemed willing to listen.
“Oh, you were close?”
“I don’t really know. It just wasn’t painful being with them.”
As a soldier fighting Gijuu on the ground and surviving, you move through many squads.
Some were uncomfortable, and sometimes I found them annoying.
Many teased me about my background, including superiors, and ignoring them wasn’t an option.
But... the last squad was different.
“The squad leader liked training and often invited me. Looking back, I think he was considerate of me, who didn’t fit in well.”
“A good leader. So, was there anyone you were especially close to?”
“I don’t know if we were close, but I spent a lot of time with ‘Shy Boy.’”
“...Shy Boy?”
Lieutenant Hayase tilted her head in confusion, so I explained the infantry call signs.
“That’s his call sign. We called each other by call signs in the squad. By the way, the squad leader’s call sign was ‘Protein.’”
Hearing our call signs, Lieutenant Hayase made a strange face.
“Those are... unique call signs.”
“Yes. The leader liked training and always carried protein. As for Shy Boy, it’s because he was shy and couldn’t talk to strangers. I’m not very talkative either, so I often stayed with Shy Boy.”
We were both quiet, and when choosing bunk beds, we somehow picked the same one.
The others were noisy, so Shy Boy probably chose the quiet me.
“It wasn’t unpleasant being together, but Shy Boy loved mint-flavored emergency rations, which was a problem.”
“Mint flavor? Did you fight over it?”

“No. When emergency rations were distributed before battle, if there was mint flavor, everyone would push it onto Shy Boy because it was so bad. It was a matter of preference, but most treated it as a dud.”
“Then it’s not a problem, right?”

“The problem starts here. When Shy Boy wanted to thank someone on the battlefield, he offered mint-flavored emergency rations. He thought it was delicious and meant it as thanks, but I especially disliked it, so it was a problem to accept.”
On the day the squad was wiped out, Shy Boy gave me mint-flavored emergency rations.
I appreciated the sentiment, but I really disliked mint flavor.
Before I knew it, I was talking to Lieutenant Hayase about my squadmates.
I was surprised myself that a smile naturally appeared.

“MC and Hair Set were often together, talking about women. Gambler and Loser gambled with other squads at night, but Loser always lost and came to borrow money from us. Comic often drew manga alone. He said he’d become a manga artist after his military service.”
Memories of my nostalgic comrades came back, and I fixed my gaze on the parfait in front of me.

“Comic showed his manga to Shy Boy and me, asking for feedback. I didn’t understand much, but I still wonder about the continuation of the manga he was drawing. He said it was about to get exciting...”
Thinking I’d never read his manga again tightened my heart.
At the time, I didn’t care much, but now I felt unbearably lonely.
“...They were good comrades. I wish I could have let them eat this parfait.”
Lieutenant Hayase seemed to understand from my tone and didn’t ask what happened to the squad.
“I see. They were important comrades to you.”
“Yes... important...”
Tears overflowed.
Feeling pathetic in front of Lieutenant Hayase, I looked down and cried.
Tears dripped onto the table, and my hand holding the spoon trembled.
“I wanted to be with everyone more... but I’m the only one who survived!”
I had thought the reason I joined the experiment was for my own existence—to be wanted as a soldier in the Prometheus Project.
But after opening my heart to Lieutenant Hayase, I realized.
“...I wanted revenge.”
Lieutenant Hayase quietly responded to my strained answer.
“I see.”

“I’m an enhanced soldier but couldn’t protect everyone... everyone fought desperately even though they should have run away... Shy Boy resisted until the end... I... I couldn’t do anything for my comrades.”
On the day the squad was wiped out, I was unbearably frustrated.
The desire for revenge with these hands was what drove me.
“Why only me... I wish someone else had survived.”
I wanted someone else to live rather than no one.
Lieutenant Hayase scolded my wish.
“Your comrades fought desperately to keep you alive. Are you denying that?”
“Huh?”
Looking up, Lieutenant Hayase stared at me.
“Your comrades fought desperately, so you’re alive now, right? You should be grateful. If you say it would have been better if you died, your comrades won’t rest in peace.”
“That’s... true, but...”
That day, everyone was defeated by a suddenly appearing humanoid Gijuu.
But they fought to the very end.
Though scared, crying, and screaming.
Being told their efforts led me here made me hate my own regrets.
“...I don’t want my comrades to be restless.”
Reflecting on my words, Lieutenant Hayase smiled and took a bite of her parfait.
“You’re wrong from the start. Be glad you’re alive. Besides, you’ve gained the power to defeat Gijuu, right? You can avenge your comrades... Your reason to fight is clear now.”
Lieutenant Hayase’s words made me happy to know I wasn’t fighting just out of jealousy.
“That sounds better than jealousy.”
Saying that, Lieutenant Hayase showed tolerance toward my jealousy and desire for revenge.
“The reason for fighting doesn’t matter. What matters is why you fight. Those who aren’t clear about that can’t get stronger here.”
Lieutenant Hayase leaned closer to me.
“I like you. You should become my retainer.”
I didn’t understand what she meant at first.
“...Retainer?”
Lieutenant Hayase saw my reaction, put her hand to her forehead, and leaned back in her chair.
“You don’t even know that? Ah... anyway, join my squad. I was just looking for subordinates.”
Apparently, Lieutenant Hayase was recruiting me.
“...May I check with the person in charge?”
“Okay, I’ll wait for your answer.”
The conversation ended, and we resumed eating parfait together.
Enjoying the sweetness of the cream and chocolate in my mouth, I asked Lieutenant Hayase one more thing.
“So, Lieutenant Hayase, why did you care about me?”
Returning to my first question, Lieutenant Hayase hesitated a little, then looked away and answered.
“I was just curious about the person I helped.”
“—Huh? No way.”
Apparently, the one who descended before me on the day I fought the humanoid Gijuu was her.
Ignoring my surprise, Lieutenant Hayase finished her parfait.
She looked complicated and tried to forcibly change the subject.
“That’s enough about that! By the way, what was your call sign when you were infantry? Your naming sense is unique, so I want to know.”
I realized I hadn’t told her my call sign while talking about my comrades.
I answered while eating parfait.
“Cherry.”
“Pfft!?”
Lieutenant Hayase’s face turned red up to her ears, and she coughed while pounding her chest with her right hand.
...Damn. I shouldn’t have said that to a woman like Lieutenant Hayase.
A few days later.
In the principal’s office, Natsuko was talking remotely with an old friend.
Her name was Himari Lunaar—the principal of the Fifth Academy.
A woman with long pink hair loosely curled in vertical rolls, wearing a gothic dress matching her hair color.
She had a gentle, calm aura and looked to be in her mid-twenties, but like Natsuko, she was a first-generation Valkyrie.
Though both were among the few surviving first-generation Valkyries, there was no nostalgia between them.
Himari smiled but made an outrageous demand.
“I’m sorry my girl caused trouble. By the way, I want Louise back.”
“Oh, you must be joking? Your agent ran wild in my garden. I can’t just hand her over easily, you know?”
Louise had tried to stop the Prometheus Project but was currently under interrogation.
She refused to speak and it was unknown under whose orders she acted.
Natsuko wanted to clarify the facts, but Himari, also a principal, had come forward herself.
“Calling her an agent is harsh. I just sent a capable girl to the Third Academy. I never thought she’d be overlooked without being scouted by any class.”
Natsuko displayed Louise’s records on the monitor and checked her grades from middle school.
As Himari said, Louise’s grades were excellent.
Though she seemed to slack off a little, she was too talented to be buried in Class 5.

“Louise Durand... she seems to be an excellent girl. It seems she falsified her background to sneak in, but our ace didn’t like her. She said she was pretending and didn’t like her. This incident was sudden, and I don’t think she’s suited to be an agent.”
When Natsuko evaluated Louise, Himari’s mood worsened.
She seemed unwilling to continue and demanded again.
“...Return Louise. In exchange, I’ll provide multiple Third Class materials. Isn’t that enough as a trade?”
Natsuko was a little surprised but also understood.
Himari must value Louise enough to prepare multiple Third Class materials.
So Natsuko decided to push back.
“By the way, I heard you got Special Class materials in the Eurasian region? I’m more interested in those.”
Himari’s refined demeanor changed when Natsuko asked for Special Class materials.
Her smile vanished, and she glared at Natsuko expressionlessly.
“Be content with what I offer. Greed will only bring you pain.”
Himari spoke in a threatening tone, but Natsuko stood and sat on the desk.
Having fought as a first-generation Valkyrie, Natsuko was not shaken by such threats.
“If you want to deal with me, show proper sincerity. Have you forgotten that the root cause lies with you?”
“I haven’t forgotten, which is why I’m preparing Third Class materials for you. While I’m conceding, hurry up and accept the deal.”
Himari had no intention of conceding, but Natsuko shrugged.
“I don’t care either way. Even if I don’t get the materials, I’ll investigate Louise and clarify the facts.”
Thinking Natsuko wouldn’t back down, Himari sighed softly to ease the tension.
“You’re as greedy as ever. That hasn’t changed since before.”
“I don’t want to hear that from you. ...So, what will you do? I don’t care either way.”
When Natsuko asked, Himari raised both hands in surrender.
Apparently, she would accept Natsuko’s demands.
“I’ll send someone to pick her up, and at that time, I’ll hand over the Special Class materials. ...If you hurt Louise even a little, I won’t forgive you.”
Natsuko was surprised her demands were accepted but also understood.
(Still the same as always.)
Hiding her thoughts, Natsuko showed happiness.
“Yes, from here on, I promise not to harm her under my name. I won’t take responsibility for any injuries before her detention, though.”
“Ha, fine. By the way—”
After the deal, Himari changed the topic.
“I hear you’re cooperating with the Prometheus Project. Natsuko, I never thought you’d be that foolish.”
Looking at Himari’s cold eyes, Natsuko shrugged.
“I only provided the location and facilities. I thought it would help the female students develop immunity to men.”
“If you continue to cooperate, be prepared. Other academies oppose the Prometheus Project. You’ll become even more isolated.”
Other academies clearly opposed militarizing men.
Even hearing that, Natsuko had no intention of changing her policy.
“I’ll continue independently. But if you want help, say so. Unlike you, I’ll lend a hand without factional ties.”
Himari sensed Natsuko wouldn’t stop supporting the project and kept her cold gaze.
“I’ll send someone to pick her up soon.”
After the call ended, Natsuko stretched in the now quiet principal’s office.
“You’re still busy with political strife. I envy your composure.”
Getting off the desk, Natsuko picked up the documents detailing the Prometheus Project.
The unexpected experimental machine had achieved an unforeseen victory, destroying many Second Class Gijuu.
Natsuko couldn’t help but feel excited.
“The organization will get noisy from now on. This will be fun.”
(The End of Volume 1)
